question.text: A solid sphere of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></math> has a charge <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></math> distributed in its volume with a charge density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>kr</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></msup></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></math> are constants and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></math> is the distance from its centre. If the electric field at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac></math> times that at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></math>, then find the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></math>

solution.text:
From Gauss' theorem,
